newsitem.title: FRANCE: Casino rises on merger speculation.
newsitem.headline: Casino rises on merger speculation.

text.p: Shares in retailer Casino were sharply higher on Friday after the chairman of rival Promodes raised the prospect of an alliance with another French retailer, brokers said.
Analysts said Casino, which had taken initial steps toward a tie-up with Promodes in the early 1990s, might be the ideal candidate.
Casino's stock was up 11.40 francs at 219.40, while Promodes shares were up 1.67 percent at 1,397 francs at 1430 GMT.

A merger would create the biggest French food retailer with 18.4 percent of the market, ahead of privately-owned Leclerc with 15.2 percent, Intermarche, also private, with 15.1 percent, Carrefour with 13.1 percent, and newly merged Auchan/Docks de France with 12.8 percent.
Analysts speculated that any deal between Promodes and Casino would be carried out through a share exchange.
They said the possibility that Promodes may be in the mood for a merger was heightened by its retreat last month from Germany with the sale of its money-losing Promohypermarkt unit.

Promodes chairman Paul-Louis Halley said in an interview with the newspaper Les Echos that he expected the French retail industry to consolidate, resulting in a market dominated by five big retail groups.
He said Promodes continues to seek both internal and external growth. But he said the group disliked hostile bids, much as it would have liked an alliance with Docks de France.

In the interview, Halley described the controlling shareholder of Casino, Jean-Charles Naouri, as an appealing person one could talk to. "His alliance with Casino was very beneficial for both parties," he said.
"When you see Casino's stock before (the deal with Naouri) and after, you see the market's homage to him," Halley was quoted as saying.
